main_text.p: Cap.i.Cap.ii.ñem confumit. Paulus Ægineta libro de re Medica quarto, & Actuarius fecundo Methodi medédi, utrunq; affectum perfpicuè discernunt. Nam qui à fæce fanguinis originem habet, is in principio fubruber eft, & mitior quodammodo, qui tàdem in nigrorem conuertitur: alter, qui à bile adusta nascitur malignior est, & totum corpus exulcerat, extremasque partes decidere facit. His addit Actuarius fuperciliorum mentiqúe pilorum defluuia affectum præcedere, & tumores in facie extuberates, oculosq; alio & alio colore notari, ac uocem exafpe rari:uenas item fub lingua turgidas, & quæ antea huiusmodi non essent, nigras efficiunt. Quòd uerò ad ætatem pertinet, pueros cū hoc morbo non conflictari, donec pubescere incipiant satis docet experientia. Regio autem huic malo opportuna ea eft, quæ uel percalida eft, uel supra modum frigida, eò quòd hæc fanguinem incrasset, refrigeretque, perspirationes prohibeat, ac denique insitum calorem opprimat: illa uerò, quòd ipsum sanguinem adasset. Propterea Galenus libro ad Glauconem secundo ait pluri mos in Alexandria ob crassam victus rationem, atq; regionis feruorem elephantiasi corripi:

page.notes: The first word "ñem" is a fragment with a tilde over the n, kept as printed. The catchword "P" stands alone on the line after "elephantiasi" at the left, under the text; it is probably a printer's mark or catchword and is doubtful. The reading "fubruber" and "perfpicuè" are as printed. The word "tàdem" has a grave accent as printed. The ligature in "Actuarius" and the long s in "fuperciliorum" and "fecundo" are transcribed with plain s.
